title: Fundcraft Secures €12m Strategic Growth Financing to Scale Digital Fund Operations Infrastructure for European Alternative Investment Funds
summary:
Fundcraft, Europe’s digital fund operations provider for alternative investment funds, today announced that it has secured €12 million in strategic growth financing co-led by Riverside Acceleration Capital (“RAC”) and CCAP Investments (“CCAP”), with participation from existing investors including 3VC, MiddleGame Ventures and Aperture Capital. The new financing brings fundcraft’s total capital secured since its founding to €40 million, reinforcing its position among Europe’s best-capitalised digital fund operations providers for alternative investment funds.
The financing further deepens fundcraft’s existing partnership with Riverside Acceleration Capital, the growth-stage investment strategy of The Riverside Company, following RAC’s earlier support for fundcraft’s expansion into France. RAC brings growth capital and operational resources to support the company’s next phase of international scale.
The round follows a period of strong and accelerating execution, as fund operations reach a clear digital inflection point. Nearly four in every five asset servicers identify manual workflows and lack of standardisation as their main operational hurdle, underscoring the pressure on legacy operating models as fund structures, investor volumes and regulatory requirements become more complex. Fundcraft is addressing this shift through a digital operating model underpinned by workflow automation and AI, designed to deliver greater control, transparency and service quality at scale. The platform today supports more than 20,000 LP subscriptions across nearly 300 funds.
In the first half of 2026, fundcraft signed as many new clients as in the whole of 2025. This momentum has been supported by successful large-scale fund migrations and continued up-market traction. Over half of new clients were mid-to-large alternative asset managers modernising their operating models or complex, multi-jurisdictional private market access platforms. 
The financing will support fundcraft’s next phase of growth: accelerating momentum across its existing European client base and core markets, while expanding into additional jurisdictions and deepening capabilities in institutional private equity Buyout strategies. It will also support the continued execution of fundcraft’s AI strategy, building on data foundations already put in place and AI-enabled workflows currently deployed across selected processes. These capabilities are being embedded across investor, fund and portfolio operations to improve operating leverage and make increasingly complex private markets strategies more scalable, transparent and economically viable.
Fundcraft’s expansion into France has moved rapidly from regulatory approval to commercial execution. After a successful implementation in Luxembourg, fundcraft Group obtained a separate AIFM license in France. This new AIFM was granted by the AMF authorisation in June 2026, and fundcraft has since been mandated to support several French fund launches, representing ambitions of more than €1 billion in combined commitments and subscription targets. Its French platform is also supporting high-volume Private Markets Access structures, including ELTIF 2.0, evergreen and open-ended funds for multi-distributor and cross-border distribution, while fundcraft increasingly supports multi-jurisdiction parallel fund setups across Luxembourg, France, the US and Spain.

title: Mastercard and Backbase Announce Strategic Collaboration to Accelerate AI-Native Banking Transformation

Mastercard and Backbase are collaborating to help financial institutions strengthen customer engagement, enhance decision-making and advance their digital transformation ambitions through a combination of data insights, cybersecurity and banking technology capabilities.
Through the collaboration, financial institutions will be able to access Mastercard capabilities that support personalization, analytics, customer engagement and cyber resilience alongside the Backbase AI-native Banking Operating System, helping them deliver more connected banking experiences and drive business growth.
As financial institutions continue to modernize their operations and customer experiences, the collaboration provides access to capabilities that support personalization, analytics, customer engagement, and cyber resilience. Key capabilities available through the collaboration include:
Dynamic Yield by Mastercard, which can support personalization and customer engagement across digital banking journeys.
Test & Learn, which can help financial institutions assess the commercial impact of product, pricing, campaign, and customer experience changes.
SpendingPulse, which can provide macroeconomic and sector-level spending insights to support business decision-making.
Cyber Quant, which can support cyber risk assessment and resilience conversations with financial institutions.

title: AXON Expands to North America With FINTRAC Registration
summary:
AXON, a financial infrastructure company building an orchestration layer for banks, fintechs and businesses, announced today that its Canadian entity, AXON TECHNOLOGY INC., is registered with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as a Money Services Business (MSB). 
The registration establishes a regulatory foundation for AXON’s operations in Canada as the company develops its international financial infrastructure. 
FINTRAC’s public registry lists foreign exchange, money transferring, virtual currency and payment service provider activities. As a registered MSB, AXON’s Canadian entity operates within Canada’s federal anti-money laundering and anti-terrorist financing framework, including applicable compliance, identification, monitoring, reporting and record-keeping obligations. 
Building infrastructure for a multi-rail financial system 
Traditional banking now operates alongside card and local payment networks, instant payment systems, stablecoins and digital-asset infrastructure. While financial institutions have more ways to move and settle money, operating across multiple providers, systems and markets creates additional complexity. 
AXON is building a single orchestration layer through which banks, fintechs and businesses can connect to and manage these different financial operations. 
Rather than requiring institutions to integrate and manage separate infrastructure for each provider or financial rail, AXON gives customers one environment to build, route, settle and control financial operations across markets, networks and technologies. The platform is designed to work with existing financial infrastructure without requiring institutions to adopt a single blockchain, stablecoin or proprietary payment network. 
“Banks don’t need to become crypto companies to access the benefits of digital assets or new financial rails,” said Malek Alzubi, Co-Founder & CEO of AXON. “They need infrastructure that lets them connect to these systems compliantly, while preserving the controls, relationships and operating models they already rely on. Our Canadian Money Services Business registration strengthens the regulatory foundation needed to connect traditional and digital finance across markets.”
Building infrastructure across markets 
The Canadian registration forms part of AXON’s broader strategy to build financial infrastructure capable of operating across jurisdictions while accommodating the regulatory, banking and liquidity requirements of individual markets. 
AXON has also signed Pulsar Money as its first Neobank Design Partner and designated banking partner covering the UAE and European markets, providing an additional foundation for the company’s expansion across multiple jurisdictions. 
AXON’s platform is designed to allow institutions to add new providers, financial rails and jurisdictions through one operating layer, helping them launch products, expand into new markets, and manage fragmented financial infrastructure without rebuilding their operational stack market by market. 
The milestone comes as AXON moves from platform development toward commercial deployment, expanding its regulatory footprint and institutional partnerships across multiple markets. The company is currently completing a $5 million Seed round to support its next phase of growth.

content: Financial infrastructure company AXON announced that its Canadian entity is now registered with FINTRAC as a Money Services Business, establishing a regulatory foundation for operations in Canada. The company is building an orchestration layer to help banks and businesses connect traditional and digital financial systems across markets without overhauling their existing infrastructure.

title: MoonPay Obtains Electronic Money Institution Licence in the Netherlands
summary:
MoonPay Europe has received its Electronic Money Institution (EMI) license from the Dutch Central Bank in the Netherlands.
Why this matters
The EMI license opens up significant new ground for MoonPay in Europe:
Custodial payment flows. MoonPay can offer payment accounts and related payment services to consumers and business customers.
Stablecoin issuance. The license allows MoonPay to issue stablecoins, which enables MoonPay to enter the euro-denominated stablecoins market.
This also places MoonPay among a small group of Dutch-based companies that can issue open-loop stablecoins from the Netherlands, alongside Quantoz. It makes MoonPay the third Netherlands-based company to hold both a MiCA Crypto-Asset Service Provider (CASP) authorization and an EMI license within a single entity. More notably, MoonPay is the first of these companies to combine both licenses in one entity while also holding open-loop stablecoin issuance capabilities, giving us broader options from the Netherlands than others in this category.
This is not MoonPay's first regulatory milestone in Europe. MoonPay was also one of the first companies to obtain a MiCAR CASP license, back in 2024, giving us one of the longest track records of any stablecoin issuer operating under Europe's regulatory framework.

The appointment follows the recent launch of Rimes’ Intelligence Fabric for Capital Markets, the company’s unified data and intelligence architecture designed to help asset owners, asset managers and asset servicers make better decisions and scale faster with AI-enabled data and workflows.

His background helping technology businesses scale rapidly, combined with his strong financial and operational expertise, will be a tremendous asset as we accelerate investment in innovation, supporting the increasing demands of our global clients, and scale the business.”
As Chief Financial Officer, Mirza will lead Rimes’ global finance organization, with responsibility spanning growth strategy, capital allocation and operational performance. As Best Buy continues to advance its digital commerce business, the company is modernizing the payments infrastructure behind it. Teaming up with Checkout.com gives Best Buy a flexible foundation to extend its reach to a broader seller base.
Through this work, Checkout.com will provide card acquiring and debit routing capabilities, supported by flexible payments technology built to adapt as Best Buy’s needs evolve. This will support Best Buy Marketplace’s current payment flows while giving its team a foundation for future payment methods, geographies, and commerce models.
Checkout.com will deliver dedicated enterprise support and industry expertise to help Best Buy navigate the complexities of various digital channels and settlement flows.
Antoine Nougué, Chief Revenue Officer at Checkout.com, comments: “Best Buy has built a trusted experience to help customers navigate increasingly complex technology purchases. We’re proud to support the next phase of that evolution with modular technology, AI-powered payment optimization, and a hands-on approach to continued innovation and growth.”
